title: 2011 HMMT November General Problem 1
statement: Find all ordered pairs of real numbers \((x, y)\) such that \(x^{2} y=3\) and \(x+x y=4\).

solutions.text:
\((1,3),\left(3, \frac{1}{3}\right)\) Multiplying the second equation by \(x\) gives

\[x^{2}+x^{2} y=4 x\]

and substituting our known value of \(x^{2} y\) gives the quadratic

\[x^{2}-4 x+3=0\]

so \(x=1\) or \(x=3\). Hence, we obtain the solutions \((x, y)=(1,3),(3,1 / 3)\).
